question: A parcel hub's regional figure is 8 times a depot's figure, expressed in kilojoules. A depot's figure covers 12 identical chutes, and each chute handles 5 parcels at a time. One parcel has a mass of 13000 g. Its speed, in metres per second, is the smaller of the two values whose square, minus 4 times the value, plus 3, comes to exactly 0. What is the hub's regional figure, in kJ?
Parameter x^2 - 4x + 3 = 0; smaller root times 4 equals 4. A 27-kilogram load at 4 m/s has energy. Convert to kilojoules, add 26, subtract 9. Position: front, not needed. What is the energy in kJ?
Parameter x^2 - 10x + 21 = 0; smaller root. A 191-kilogram system at this acceleration generates force. Subtract 20, subtract 1, subtract 14. Version: 2.1, not applicable. What is the force in N?

A calibration check for a buoy's speed sensor requires two candidate readings, in meters per second, whose sum is 12 and whose product is 35; the smaller of the two is always used. This is the speed of an 11,000 gram sensor float; find its kinetic energy, convert to kilojoules, multiply by 11 for an eleven-buoy array, add 3 kilojoules for a shared baseline offset, and multiply the whole total by 7 for seven days of data. What is the total energy, in kilojoules, after seven days?

The value to report is a signed energy balance in kJ, gains positive: one cart's net figure in kJ, minus 8 kJ consumed by the launcher, multiplied by 11 because 11 identical carts are launched. A cart has a mass of 32000 g and position 3t³ + 0t² metres along its rail, with t in seconds. Its net figure is its energy of motion at its speed at t = 1 s, less 7 J of rail friction, converted to kJ. What is the balance, in kJ?

A load distribution is found by integrating 3x² over the range from x = 2 to x = 4 meters. This integral represents a velocity in m/s for a 60 kg mass. The kinetic energy is calculated. Subtracting 3 J for calibration gives an adjusted energy. This is amplified 12 times through a power system. The result is amplified 10 times more through a secondary stage. Finally, it is amplified by 3 times through the foundation. What is the final kinetic energy in J? (The mass's color is red, which does not apply.)

The final figure in a drone-hangar report, in kN, is a combined thrust expressed in kN minus a 20 kN tie-down load, with the thrust direction positive, so it may be negative. The combined thrust is that of 12 hangars each holding 12 drones, so it is the single-drone thrust multiplied by 12 and then by 12. A single drone supplies the thrust needed to accelerate its 6,000 g body at a rate in m/s² equal to the greatest common divisor of 299 and 267. What is the final figure, in kN?

Solving x² - 9x + 20 = 0 with larger root 5 m/s² acceleration. A 142 kg load produces force. Decreased by 6 N, decreased by 16 N, increased by 3 N, and multiplied by 12. The load color is black but is not used. What is the final force in N?

Solving x² - 10·x + 16 = 0, smaller root is 2 m/s. With 25 kg, energy = 0.5 × 25 × 4 = 50 J, increased by 4, reduced by 25, scaled by 3, converted to kilojoules. The room lighting is 500 lux, not used. What is the final energy in kilojoules?

A depot audit ends with a single energy figure in kilojoules. A skip of mass 52 kg travels along the rail at a speed, in metres per second, worked out as 8 multiplied by the sum of 4 and 1. The energy the moving skip carries is the base amount. To that the auditor adds 30 J already stored in the buffer spring. A train holds 12 skips, so a train carries 12 times the corrected amount, and the depot dispatches 9 such trains. What is the depot figure, in kJ?

The result the lab wants is a signed net force in kN, forward positive: a probe's forward force converted to kN, minus a 14 kN retarding clamp. The probe has a mass of 2 kg and sits on a bench 1.6 m wide. Its acceleration, in m/s², is 11 times the largest whole number that divides both 206 and 325 with no remainder. The forward force is what is needed to produce that acceleration, plus a 4 N push from a spring. What is the net signed force, in kN?

The total thrust a launch crew records, in N, is 4 times the thrust of a single booster. A single booster supplies exactly the force needed to accelerate a 19,000 g test payload at a certain rate. That rate, in m/s², is obtained by starting from 8 times the sum of 9 and 8, then subtracting 28, then subtracting 13, and finally subtracting 23. What total thrust does the crew record, in N?

A lab's final energy reading, in kilojoules after a final sixfold scaling, is wanted — but it starts with two rod lengths. Two rods measure 302 cm and 41 cm; the greatest length dividing both evenly is used as the speed, in meters per second, of a slider whose mass is stated as 49000 grams. The slider's kinetic energy is converted into kilojoules, then reduced by 18 kJ, then increased by 13 kJ, and finally scaled by a factor of 6. What is the final energy, in kilojoules?

The final kilonewton total has 26 subtracted from it, after scaling a converted force fivefold. That force comes from an 11 kg test block and its acceleration, which is the number of different ways to choose 4 of 8 distinct calibration bolts, without regard to order, minus 9 newtons for a mounting correction applied after the force itself is found. A separate voltmeter nearby reads 9 volts, unrelated to this calculation. What is the final force, in kilonewtons?

A cyclist and bike with a combined mass of 55,000 g ride at a speed in m/s equal to the number of ways to choose 2 riders from a squad of 8. A team of 8 such riders has a combined energy of motion 8 times that of one rider. Four teams race, so the race figure is 4 times the team figure. From the race figure, 13 J of timing-gate loss is subtracted. What is the resulting figure, in J?
The GCD of 258 and 342, plus 1, scaled by 9, minus 2, minus 11, gives velocity for 51 kg kinetic energy. What is the final energy in Joules?

Integral of 1·x² + 7·x from 0 to 4 is 90.67 m/s velocity. With 59 kg, energy = 0.5 × 59 × 8221 J, reduced by 14, converted to kilojoules, increased by 14, scaled by 6. The observer's name is John, not relevant. What is the final energy in kilojoules?

The final action on this test bench's readout is always to convert its newton figure into kilonewtons — that happens right at the end. A wrecking-ball rig used to demolish an old structure carries a wrecking ball of mass 172 kilograms. An operator takes 5 units, adds 9 units, multiplies that sum by 7, then subtracts 29 from the result — this final number is the ball's swing acceleration, in meters per second squared, at the point of impact. Using that acceleration and the ball's mass, the impact force is found. Because the rig strikes twice in that pass, the force is doubled, and a structural correction then subtracts 6 from the doubled value. The demolition site is fenced off across 40 meters. Finally, exactly as noted at the start, the result is converted from newtons to kilonewtons. What is the final force, in kilonewtons?

A rate function 1*x^2 + 7*x is integrated from x = 1 to x = 2, then increased by 13 to yield a velocity in m/s. A 59 kg object at this velocity stores energy, converted to kilojoules, with 15 kilojoules added, 28 subtracted. A light wavelength of 550 nanometers was measured but does not apply. What is the final energy in kilojoules?

A power system combines 2 configurations from 10 available (10 choose 2 = 45), with this velocity in m/s applied to an 18 kg mass. Kinetic energy is calculated, converted to kJ, amplified 11 times through generation, 5 times through power conditioning, and 12 times through distribution. What is the total available power in kJ?

A function f(x) = 4*x^3 + 6*x^2 has second derivative at x = 2 giving acceleration 36 m/s^2. A 54-kilogram object at 36 m/s has kinetic energy calculated from half mass times velocity squared. Convert from joules to kilojoules, subtract 6, multiply by 7, and multiply by 12. What is the final energy in kilojoules?

At a winch drum station, the last action taken is to multiply a kilonewton reading by 5 before logging the final tally. That reading traces back to a motor whose output rate r(t) follows r(t) = 1 times t squared plus 8 times t (in units per second), between t = 3 seconds and t = 4 seconds; the total amount accumulated over that interval becomes the acceleration, in meters per second squared, applied to an 86-kilogram drum. The workshop also keeps 40 liters of hydraulic fluid on hand, unrelated to this measurement. This produces a push measured in newtons, which is then increased by 16, multiplied by 5, converted from newtons into kilonewtons, and finally multiplied by the 5 mentioned first. What is the final push, in kilonewtons?

A velocity integration test computes from integral of x² + 6x from 0 to 4 (yielding 109.33 m/s). A 36 kg mass accelerates at this rate to yield energy, converted to kilojoules, increased by 27 kJ, further increased by 20 kJ, and finally reduced by 25 kJ. What is the final energy in kilojoules?

A container terminal needs the net figure, in kilonewtons, for a spreader trial. The spreader's rate of change of speed a, in m/s^2, is the smaller value satisfying a^2 - 12a + 35 = 0. The spreader has a mass of 174000 g, and the hoist supplies exactly the force needed to produce that motion. That force is expressed in kilonewtons, and the terminal runs 10 identical spreaders. A standing gantry relief of 20 kN is subtracted from their combined figure, and a lashing pre-load of 2 kN is then added. What is the net figure, in kN?

The total in a shipyard's winch report, in N, is 5 times a dock total. The dock total is 10 times a bay total, and the bay total is 7 times a single-winch pull. A single winch supplies the force needed to accelerate a 66 kg anchor block at a rate in m/s² equal to the area under y = 4x² + 6x between x = 1 and x = 2. The winch cable is 30 m long. What is the total in the report, in N?
